guide.summary: Private app on your own workspace (self-serve, wait none); Public app for other companies (unlisted) (app review); Public app listed in the Intercom App Store (app review).
guide.verdict: Easiest: Private app on your own workspace (self-serve, wait none). Hardest: Public app for other companies (unlisted) (app review).

composio.note: Composio lists a managed OAuth app for Intercom, so prototypes need no own app. Create a custom auth config with your own client ID and secret for production.

need_own_app.answer: Not for prototypes, since Composio provides a managed Intercom app. For production, use your own app if users should see your brand, you need your own scopes, or you want dedicated quota.
reasons: Users should see your app name instead of Composio on the consent screen
Managed apps share quota across all Composio users; your own app gets dedicated quota
Default scopes of a managed app may not include everything you need
Managed auth enforces a 15-minute minimum polling interval

scenarios.label: Private app on your own workspace
scenarios.when_this_applies: Your agent only accesses data in your own paid Intercom workspace.

hands_on.basis: estimate from step count, not measured

waiting.basis: Private apps on your own paid workspace need no review (c4).

scenarios.approval: No review is required for private apps accessing only your own paid workspace data.

scenarios.label: Public app for other companies (unlisted)
scenarios.when_this_applies: Customers outside your company install your app via OAuth from your own product or site.

hands_on.basis: estimate from step count, not measured; includes recording the video and filling in the listing and partner forms (c13, c24)

waiting.basis: No verified source backs this timeline (the agent's estimate was "Up to 7 business days per submission").

scenarios.approval: Intercom reviews the app, its scopes, a demo video and listing details before it can be installed by others. Unlisted apps must also be submitted for review.

modifiers.note: During review the app is private to your team
Changes to an approved app need re-approval

extras: During review the app is private to your
Changes to an approved app need re-approval

scenarios.label: Public app listed in the Intercom App Store
scenarios.when_this_applies: You also want customers to discover and install the app from the Intercom App Store.

hands_on.basis: estimate from step count, not measured; adds listing assets (c14-c18)

waiting.basis: No verified source backs this timeline (the agent's estimate was "Up to 7 business days per submission").

scenarios.approval: Same review as unlisted, with an App Store listing that must meet all requirements before submission.

prerequisites.title: Paid Intercom workspace (private app)
prerequisites.detail: Access tokens for private apps need your own paid workspace.

prerequisites.title: Terms of service, privacy policy, support email, docs URL
HTTPS redirect URLs
prerequisites.detail: Redirect URLs must use HTTPS. You can register several, including test and production URLs.

prerequisites.title: Test account or setup instructions
prerequisites.detail: If your service needs an account, give reviewers test credentials or instructions.

steps.title: Create auth config with managed app (prototype)
steps.detail: Use Composio's managed Intercom app to prototype without your own app.
steps.done_when: A test user can connect Intercom.

steps.title: Enable OAuth in Developer Hub
steps.detail: Tick Use OAuth on the Authentication page and pick scopes by checkbox.
steps.done_when: OAuth is on and scopes are selected.

steps.title: Draft minimal scope list and justification
steps.detail: Choose only the scopes the use case needs; over-privileged scopes are the top rejection reason.
steps.done_when: Scope list maps each scope to a feature.

steps.title: Copy Composio redirect URI into app
steps.detail: Copy the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard into the Intercom redirect URLs. It must be HTTPS.
steps.done_when: Redirect URL is saved in Developer Hub.

steps.title: Create Composio auth config with own credentials
steps.detail: Use client_id and client_secret from the Basic Information page via Composio's API.
steps.done_when: Auth config exists with your credentials.

steps.title: Prepare listing text and images
steps.detail: Draft name, descriptions, categories and image specs to the listing rules, without the word Intercom in the name.
steps.done_when: All required listing fields are drafted.

steps.title: Provide legal, company and listing details
steps.detail: Supply terms and privacy URLs, company details, points of contact and complete the App Partner Program form.
steps.done_when: Listing and partner pages are complete.

steps.title: Record the review video
steps.detail: Show OAuth install, the end-to-end experience and OAuth uninstall, with full client_id and state in the OAuth URL.

steps.title: Submit for review
steps.detail: Use Submit for Review in the Test and publish section of the Developer Hub.

steps.title: Wait for Intercom review
steps.detail: Review can take up to seven business days; a rejection means fixing and resubmitting.
steps.done_when: App is approved as public unlisted.

steps.title: Set listing live in App Store
steps.detail: After approval, select List in App store on the listing page.
steps.done_when: App appears in the App Store.

steps.title: Give customers install instructions
steps.detail: Unlisted apps must be installed through your own product or website.
steps.done_when: Customers can start the OAuth install from your product.

traps.title: Over-broad scopes cause rejection
traps.detail: This is the most common reason for initial rejection. Intercom may ask you to adjust scopes and resubmit.

traps.title: App is private while in review
traps.detail: Only you and your team can use the app during review, so real customers cannot connect yet.

traps.title: Unlisted apps still need review
traps.detail: Skipping the App Store listing does not skip the review.

traps.title: Broken install links or bad images
traps.detail: Broken or unclear installation links lead to rejection. Images not in marketing format are a common pitfall.

traps.title: Name and logo rules
traps.detail: The app name cannot contain Intercom and the icon cannot contain the Intercom logo.

traps.title: Updates need re-approval
traps.detail: The published app keeps its current functionality until updates are approved.

blockers.what_it_means: The review found problems such as extra scopes, broken links or listing issues.
blockers.what_to_do: Make the requested changes and resubmit; allow up to seven more business days.
blockers.agent_can_help: Re-check the scope list against features and verify links and listing specs.

open_questions: Is there a developer docs landing URL and any Composio credential guide for Intercom? Check developers.intercom.com and the Composio Intercom toolkit page.
Is there any measured review turnaround beyond the documented seven business days? Ask Intercom developer support or check community reports.
Are there per-customer admin requirements to install an OAuth app? Not found; test with a customer workspace or ask Intercom support.

evidence.question: G2
